notes:
Ink layers stay with the piece they belong to.

**An ink layer created for one piece could appear on others.** While two tablets were paired, the layer one tablet was using could be applied to whatever piece the other tablet happened to have open — and remembered there. That meant markings drawn afterwards were filed under a layer belonging to a different piece, and appeared to have vanished. Layers now travel with the piece they belong to and are ignored if they arrive for anything else.

**Layers a piece never uses are tidied away.** A piece's layer list only ever grew. It is now cleaned up when the piece opens, keeping any layer that actually has markings on it, the Default layer, and whichever layer that piece was last set to. Markings are never touched.

**Deleting a layer now deletes what was drawn on it.** Previously it removed the layer from the list but left the markings, so the layer reappeared the next time the piece was opened. The confirmation now tells you exactly how many marks will be deleted, and only that piece is affected.

If markings seem to be missing from a piece, check its ink layer — they are most likely on another one.

Your library, annotations and licence are not affected.
